item.p: Scanner (, by hand): sxml_csv_read_token gives one (field, row end, input end; glossary) per call and keeps its place in a , a plain value: no object, no allocation. A field is a view into the text; only a quoted field with a doubled quote or a CR needs sxml_csv_decode_field, into caller memory no longer than the field. Special characters are matched as whole UTF-8 sequences byte by byte.

Rules where F&O 4.0 is loose: CR is a newline, so it cannot be a separator, quote or comment marker (FOCV0002, like LF); trimming removes U+0020 and U+0009 from unquoted fields and all four XML whitespace characters from header names; with trim-rows, a blank row is padded to the first row's width like any short row; select-columns beyond a header's end name the zero-length string; a selected position past int64_t selects nothing.
fn:csv-to-arrays is not implemented: F&O 4.0 dropped it (issue 2961, absorbed into fn:parse-csv) and QT4 has no test set for it.

One parse, three functions: fn:parse-csv builds columns, column index and rows once; the record's get is a function item over a static row (after fn:regex, ) capturing rows and column index, signature from the record's field type. fn:csv-to-xml walks that result, as the specification defines it over fn:parse-csv. fn:csv-doc calls the fn:unparsed-text row (found by name, as fn:json-doc finds parse-json), so text decoding () is written once.

Measured (release driver, XP40, passed of cases; before at 3a3a3cb, all wrong errors): fn-parse-csv 35 to 107/124, fn-csv-to-xml 9 to 68/68 run, fn-csv-doc 4 to 20/20. The 17 parse-csv failures are assertions such as ?get(1, 1) = "one" that read the result as the context value, which the driver does not bind (Proposed below); with it, 124/124.
